body:
#1596 removed `cd /app/calibre-web-automated` from both s6 units, so the service
now runs with the Dockerfile's WORKDIR /config.

Anything anchored to BASE_DIR, __file__, or CALIBRE_DBPATH is unaffected —
templates, translations, static assets, app.db, gdrive.db, logging and dirs.json
all still resolve correctly, which is why the container boots and CI is green.

What changes is any stored *relative* path, which now resolves against /config
rather than the app root:

  - config_calibre_dir (cps/db.py) — os.path.join preserves a relative base, so
    a relative library path points somewhere new
  - TLS certfile/keyfile (cps/server.py)
  - a relative CACHE_DIR override
  - the admin path chooser's os.getcwd() fallback (cps/admin.py), whose starting
    directory changes from the app root to /config
  - relative -p/-g/-c/-k/-o CLI values (the units pass none, so not a container
    concern)

Docker installs overwhelmingly store absolute paths (/calibre-library), so this
is unlikely to be hit, and no reporter has hit it. Recorded rather than fixed
because the failure mode for anyone who did store a relative library path is a
library that silently stops resolving after an upgrade, which is expensive to
diagnose from the symptom.

If it ever surfaces: resolve stored relative paths against BASE_DIR at read
time, or normalise them to absolute on save.
title: Dropping the s6 chdir moves relative stored paths from the app root to /config
